title: Routine Cell Culture
author: Sean Misek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.q2jdycn

steps.title: Prepare Complete Growth Media
steps.instruction: Prepare the growth medium by mixing DMEM, FBS, and Anti/Anti.

substeps.instruction: Mix 1 bottle (500 mL) of DMEM with 50 mL of FBS and 5 mL of Anti/Anti.
Shake to mix.
Store in the fridge for several weeks/months.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Materials
steps.instruction: Pre-warm reagents and organize materials in the tissue culture hood.

substeps.instruction: Remove growth media and trypsin-EDTA from the fridge and pre-warm in a water bath for 10-15 minutes.
Wipe bottles with 70% ethanol and move to the hood.
Clean a bottle of sterile PBS (stored at room temperature) and move to the hood.
Move required tissue culture plastics (e.g., 10 cm or 6-well plates) into the hood.

steps.title: Inspect Cell Confluence and Contamination
steps.instruction: Verify the state of the cells before passaging.

substeps.instruction: Remove the plate from the incubator.
Visually inspect for appropriate confluence (typically ~75%); discard and thaw a new vial if overconfluent.
Inspect under high power magnification to ensure no obvious contamination.
Move the plate to the cell culture hood.

steps.title: Wash Cells with PBS
steps.instruction: Rinse the cells using Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS, pH 7.4, Fisher Scientific #10010-049).

substeps.instruction: Add PBS to the wall of the plate.
Swirl the plate.
Remove the PBS, ensuring cells do not dry out.

steps.title: Detach Cells using Trypsin
steps.instruction: Trypsinize the cells to detach them from the plate.

substeps.instruction: Add Trypsin-EDTA (0.25%, STEMCELL Technologies #7901) to the plate (volume appropriate for a 10-cm plate).
Incubate at room temperature for approximately 2 minutes (or at 37°C/longer if required for specific cell lines).
Inspect cells; if still stuck, tap the plate or incubate longer.

steps.title: Neutralize Trypsin and Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Stop the trypsinization process and create a cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Add complete media to the plate (volume appropriate for a 10-cm plate).
Pipette up and down to break up cell clumps.

steps.title: Seed Cells into New Plate
steps.instruction: Transfer a portion of the cell suspension to a new culture vessel.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL of complete media to a new 10-cm cell culture plate.
Add an appropriate amount of cell suspension to the new plate (typically 1 mL for most cell lines).
Use the remaining cell suspension for experiments or discard it.
